addresses.name: CVictoryConditionItem::CVictoryConditionItem
addresses.signature: CVictoryConditionItem* __stdcall CVictoryConditionItem::CVictoryConditionItem(void* gui@ECX, CVictoryConditionItem* this@stack:4, void* parent@stack:8) @EAX
addresses.comment: A row of `vc_list`: builds the gui window `vc_entry` through the gui system in ECX (0x1A857D8) with the parent the caller gives, finds its text `vc_name` (+0x2C) and icon `vc_info` (+0x30), and leaves condition (+0x28) nought and the shown-met byte (+0x34) nought. 0x38 bytes. `ret 8` at 0x6D1F9C. Bound to a condition afterwards by CVictoryConditionItem::SetCondition. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-endgame.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: `ret 8` at 0x6D1F9C; the call at 0x6D28D5 passes ECX = [0x1A857D8], the new object and the in-game screen's slot 16; vftable 0x15D2EF8 written at 0x6D1EFD; strings `vc_entry`, `vc_name`, `vc_info` read off the decompile and the listing. Wrong if a read of those element names disagreed with vc_interface.gui.

addresses.name: CVictoryConditionItem::SetCondition
addresses.comment: **Binds a row of `vc_list` to a condition.** Stores it (+0x28); `vc_name` = the localised text of the condition's name (+8), the whole key `GetText` of the name; then sets the shown-met byte (+0x34) to the opposite of met (+0x68) so that CVictoryConditionItem_RefreshMet always sets the frame. `ret 8` at 0x6D20AB. Two pushes at the one caller, CVictoryConditionsView::RebuildList (0x6D294E). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-endgame.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: `ret 8` at 0x6D20AB; `sete cl` at 0x6D208E into [ebx+0x34] then ESI = EBX and `call 0x6D20B0`. Shown wrong if the frame were not refreshed at bind.

addresses.name: CVictoryConditionItem_RefreshMet
addresses.comment: **A row's background follows whether its condition is met.** Where the row has a condition and met (+0x68) differs from the shown byte (+0x34): the byte is copied and `vc_entry_bg` is set (slot 18, SetFrame) to frame **1 when not met, 2 when met** (`(byte != 0) + 1`). GFX_vc_entry_bg has noOfFrames = 2, frame 1 grey and frame 2 amber (measured off vc_entry_bg.dds, 712 by 32 a frame). Bare `ret` at 0x6D2158. Called for every row once a day by CVictoryConditionsView::Update (0x6D2E65), and at the bind. Nothing else about a row changes when its condition is met, and **the date of the condition is never shown**. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-endgame.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: `push` nothing; both call sites load ESI first (0x6D2E60 `mov esi,[edi]`, 0x6D2091 `mov esi,ebx`); bare `ret` at 0x6D2158. Frame arithmetic is `(char)[esi+0x34] != 0` + 1 in the decompile. The 2 frames are noOfFrames in vc_interface.gfx.

addresses.name: VictoryConditionItem_Tooltip
addresses.comment: **The tooltip of a victory condition's row**, shared by the in-game `vc_entry` and the lobby's `condition_entry` (both keep the condition at +0x28, hence class-free): appends to `out->text` the trigger's account of itself, `CAndTrigger::GetBlockText(this, scope, redWhen = false, depth = 0)` on the condition's trigger (+0x24), with an empty scope (a CEventScope with country `---`/0). So at depth 0 an `and` draws no header and lists its conditions, each line with a red or green asterisk by whether it holds now. Called from CVictoryConditionsView_ElementTooltip and CSelectVictoryConditionsView::ElementTooltip. `ret 8` at 0x6D2225. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-endgame.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: `ret 8` at 0x6D2225; slot call `[[cond+0x24]+0x24]` (slot 9 of CAndTrigger) with (out, scope, 0, 0); both item classes' constructors store the condition at +0x28 (0x6D1FA0 and 0x71B4E0). Wrong if the lobby's entry held something else there.

addresses.name: CVictoryConditionsView::CVictoryConditionsView
addresses.signature: CVictoryConditionsView* __stdcall CVictoryConditionsView::CVictoryConditionsView(CVictoryConditionsView* this, void* screen, Hoi3CString* name) @EAX
addresses.comment: The in-game victory conditions window (`vc_window`), 0x7C bytes, made in `CInGameIdler::CInGameIdler` (at 0x64942B, new 0x7C, name 'vc_window') and kept at `CInGameIdler +0x1D48`. Stores the screen (+0x28) and the name (+0x30), sets faction (+0x2C) nought and day (+0x4C) -1, makes the close button's glue at +0x50 (handler the generic 'hide the window' at 0x7D8760), runs CVictoryConditionsView::Build and hides the window. `ret 0xC` at 0x6D234A. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-endgame.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: `ret 0xC` at 0x6D234A; `push 0x7C` at 0x6493E3 and the call at 0x64942B, the result stored to param_1[0x752] (= +0x1D48); vftable 0x15D2EC0 written at 0x6D22CA. Wrong if another 0x7C-byte view lived at +0x1D48.

addresses.name: CVictoryConditionsView::Build
addresses.comment: Slot 0, the window built again: an old window dropped (+0x20), `vc_window` made from `vc_interface.gui` through the gui system, `vc_list` found (+0x24), `close_button` hooked to the glue at +0x50, `vc_bg_allies`, `vc_bg_axis` and `vc_bg_com` hidden (slot 14), and day (+0x4C) set to -1. Answers true. Bare `ret` at 0x6D2645. `vc_nofaction_label` is named by no code at all (the string is not in the image). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-endgame.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Bare `ret` at 0x6D2645; the three names and the hide (slot 0x38) off the decompile; absent string checked with image.findBytes(b'vc_nofaction_label'), positive control the same call finding `vc_window` once.

addresses.name: CVictoryConditionsView::RebuildList
addresses.comment: **The rows of `vc_list`, for the player's faction.** Hides the list (slot 21). The faction is stored (+0x2C); the matching entry of **chosen** (conditions +0x18, not all) gives the rows: rows added (CVictoryConditionItem, slot 4) until as many as conditions, surplus rows removed from the end (slot 24), each row bound in order with CVictoryConditionItem::SetCondition, the list laid out (slot 27), and shown (slot 20). Rows are in chosen's order, so a faction's conditions in the order CChooseVictoryConditionsCommand gave them - the file's order for a start. A faction the conditions do not hold touches no row (the rows stay as they were) and the list is shown; the three tags Update reaches this for are the file's, so it does not arise in the shipped game. `ret 4` at 0x6D2985. One caller: Update. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-endgame.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: `ret 4` at 0x6D2985; slot 0x54 hide, 0x10 add, 0x60 remove (iterator walked to the wanted count at 0x6D291A), 0x6C layout and 0x50 show; slots' names from GuiListBox. Wrong if slot 24 removed from the front.

addresses.name: CVictoryConditionsView::Update
addresses.comment: **`vc_window`'s update.** Does nothing unless the window is shown (window +0x5B) and there is a player. Called each frame while shown from UpdateTutorialAndAuxWindows (0x64FF62) and once by CInGameIdler::ToggleGoals, which first sets faction (+0x2C) to 0 so the show always rebuilds. **Where the player's faction differs from +0x2C**: by its tag - `axis`, `allies`, `comintern` - its own picture is shown and the other two hidden, then RebuildList and the list shown (slot 20); any other tag (the null faction) hides all three pictures and hides the list, leaving vc_bg and `vc_nofaction_label`, which nothing touches; +0x2C is not set in that arm so it runs every frame. **Once when the day of the year changes** ((tick - 43800000) / 24 less whole years of g_DaysPerYear) and on first show (-1): VCWindow_SetFactionProgress for axis, allies and comintern (always all three, whichever faction the player is in) and each row's RefreshMet. Bare `ret` at 0x6D2E7F. **It does not pause the game**. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-endgame.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Bare `ret` at 0x6D2E7F; two callers 0x649FA2 and 0x64FF62 (findRefs); the three String_EqualsCString arms and the else arm off the decompile. Pause claim: no call to TogglePause or the pause command in the body or in ToggleGoals.

addresses.name: CSelectVictoryConditionsView::RebuildList
addresses.comment: **The lobby's list: every condition of the player's faction, in the file's order** (conditions +0x28, `all`, not `chosen`), each row ticked where its chosen byte (+0x69) is set. The list hidden (slot 21) and emptied (slot 9) first, faction stored (+0x2C); each row made and given the group `gamesetup`; laid out (slot 27). Then `vclobby_label` = VC_FACTION_HEADER '$FACTION$ Victory Conditions' with $FACTION$ the faction's localised name, and the list shown. `ret 4` at 0x71C55D. So reopening the window shows the chosen list again, and a cancelled edit is gone. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-endgame.md, section B.

addresses.name: VictoryConditions_PlayerMayChoose
addresses.comment: **Who may open the lobby's victory conditions window, and whose `victoryconditions_button` is enabled** (with no save loaded): the player's country is real and its faction valid (vf_7), and the country is the faction's first member (a real faction's leader) **or a scenario is running** (+0xD0C). So in a campaign only the faction's leader chooses. Bare `ret`s at 0x71C6EC and 0x71C700. Three callers: CGameSetup::Update (0x70C00D, the enable), OnVictoryConditionsButton (0x71AA46), CSelectVictoryConditionsView::Update (0x71C746). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-endgame.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: 0x71C658 `cmp [esi+4],edi; je` true, then 0x71C6D1 `cmp [esi+0xD0C],ebx; je` false else al=1; three callers by findRefs. Wrong if first member were not the leader (FINDINGS-factionplay.md A.3).

addresses.name: CSelectVictoryConditionsView::Update

Where the player's faction changed (the country was changed): hide, reopen and rebuild, the ticks lost. Then `info` = ticked / NUMBER_OF_VICTORY_CONDITIONS, `%d / %d`, and `§R%d§W / %d` (the count red) when they differ - the only place the window speaks of the limit. Bare `ret` at 0x71C9FF. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-endgame.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Bare `ret` at 0x71C9FF; the format at 0x15D5E58 reads '§R%d§W / %d'; hide (slot 0x38 through +0x18) when PlayerMayChoose answers no.

addresses.name: CAlertManager_VictoryConditionsTooltip
addresses.comment: **Alert 14's tooltip, whole.** `text` = VC_ALERT '§GVictory Conditions§W'. Then for every faction of the game state's list (+0xCE4) other than the player's, with met x 100 / VICTORY_CONDITIONS_TO_WIN >= 75 (9 of 12): `delayed` = VC_DANGER '§Y$FACTION$§W have completed §R$NUM$§W victory conditions.' with the faction's localised name and its met count. **Each overwrites the last, so the delayed half names only the last such faction in the list's order.** `ret 4` at 0x607ECC. addresses.name: CInGameIdler::ToggleGoals
addresses.comment: **What `menubar_goals_button` does: shows or hides the victory conditions window `vc_window`** (CVictoryConditionsView, this +0x1D48) - there is no other window behind it. Showing it (window byte +0x5B nought): Show (slot 13), raise (slot 11), its faction (+0x2C) set to nought so its update rebuilds the list, CVictoryConditionsView::Update at once, and hide the Strategic Effects window (+0x1D4C). Bound to the command at this+0xB68 (constructor, 0x247C7B), which EnterGame_SetInGame binds to menubar_goals_button (0x25DA58); also called by CInGameIdler::OnAlertClicked (0x64B298). The button's tooltip is VC_BUTTON_TOOLTIP 'Victory Conditions' (CInGameIdler_NamedElementTooltip at 0x2C4D11). 0x649F70 to the bare `ret` at 0x649FBE. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-endgame.md, section B.

The button is enabled only with no save loaded and PlayerMayChoose yes (CGameSetup::Update). Bare ret. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-endgame.md, section B.

addresses.name: CSelectVictoryConditionsView::OnAccept
addresses.comment: The lobby's victory-condition window's accept button (its CButtonObserverGlue, built at 0x71B83D). Where the player's country is real and in a valid faction: the ticked entries of the window's list (an entry's +0x2C object's +0x60 == 1), **in the list's order**, give their condition's (entry +0x28) name and FormatHourDate(+0x64); VictoryConditions_FitChoiceToCount fits them to NUMBER_OF_VICTORY_CONDITIONS; a CChooseVictoryConditionsCommand(faction, list) is posted through the session's channel; the window is hidden. Otherwise only hidden. The button itself needs nothing more, and it can only be reached through a window only the faction's first member (or anyone in a scenario) may open: VictoryConditions_PlayerMayChoose, which is what VC_BUTTON_DISABLED_INVALID 'Only countries that are faction leaders can select victory conditions.' reports on `victoryconditions_button`. **Accept is never greyed** whatever the number ticked. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-endgame.md, section B.
addresses.evidence: Decompile of 0x71B9E0 and of 0x71C560 (the opening test); no enable/disable on accept_button in Build or Update.
addresses.revises: the opening test is now read: 'any member of a faction can send its faction's choice from this button' was true of the button only, not of who reaches it.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::OnAlertClicked
addresses.comment: **Slot 80: what a click on an alert does**, by the alert's name. It closes the open side menu first. For `alert_deployable_units` it opens side menu 5, the deploy menu (CInGameIdler_OpenSideMenu). Only that arm was read; the function goes on through the other alerts. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md. **`alert_victory_conditions`** (read 2026-11-08, reversing/findings/FINDINGS-endgame.md, section B): after the side menus and orders view are closed, the goals window is opened (CInGameIdler::ToggleGoals) if it is hidden, and left alone if it is shown - so the alert only ever opens it.
